answer: A copper stake is the mesa on which agent identity stands: every agent must lock a small amount of copper-backed collateral before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if the same identity is caught mirroring itself across fake accounts. Because each Sybil copy costs real collateral and pays real slashing risk, an attacker must fund every fake the way a real agent funds itself, so creating ten thousand mirrors costs ten thousand stakes. Honest agents pay once; fakes pay per copy, which makes large-scale Sybil farming unprofitable.
